title: R_4(6(x-y)=5z) > 1500: the shell construction at the next point of the k=4 row
statement: The 4-colour Rado number of 6(x-y) = 5z exceeds 1500. The lower bound is a direct instance of the main theorem of this work at (a,b,k) = (6,5,4), which satisfies its hypotheses (a >= 2, gcd(a,b) = 1, b < a, k >= 2), so it costs no search: N = b(a^(k-1) + 2*Sigma_(k-2)) = 5*(216 + 84) = 1500. The construction predicts the exact value 1501 = 6^4 + 6^3 - 2*6 + 1, and tightness is attained at every point where a value is known on the line b = a-1 with a >= 3 and k in {3,4}. The upper bound is OPEN: no refutation of F_1501 has been attempted here. This entry is outside the published tables of Chang-De Loera-Wesley, whose four-colour Table 10 has no (a,b) = (6,5) cell.

provenance.conjectured_by: theorem: the main theorem of this work applies at (a,b,k) = (6,5,4) and yields N = 1500 with no computation; the exact value 1501 is predicted by the tightness pattern on the line b = a-1, not proved
searched_by: none: the colouring is written down from Definition 3.1 of the paper, not searched for
checked_by: shell.py, an independent reimplementation of Definition 3.1 written from the paper text and sharing no code with the ledger's generators: built the [1500] colouring and enumerated all 218,125 solution triples of 6(x-y)=5z in [1500] by direct search over (x,y) with no gcd reduction; none monochromatic
scripts/check-claim-certificates.py witness replay (a third, independent O(n^2) enumerator)
provenance.machine: linux x86-64, witness constructed and enumerated locally

prior_art.citation: Y. Chang, J. A. De Loera, W. J. Wesley, 'Rado Numbers and SAT Computations', ISSAC 2022
prior_art.establishes: R_3 and partial R_4 tables for this family; no (a,b) = (5,4) entry at k = 4. Their Lemma 4.2 is the k=3 shadow of the shell construction used here.

evidence.notes: The shell colouring of [1500] at (a,b,k) = (6,5,4), written down from the construction rather than searched for. Class sizes and the two-ended shell structure follow Definition 3.1 exactly. 218,125 solutions enumerated in [1500], none monochromatic. This fills the second of the two open cells in the k=4 row of the paper's Table 1; the first, (5,4), is rado-r4-a5-b4-frontier.

known: R_4(6(x-y)=5z) > 1500, witnessed and verified (evidence row witness-1500)
The lower bound follows from this work's main theorem with no search, the hypotheses b < a and gcd(a,b) = 1 both holding at (6,5)

The shell construction predicts 1501 exactly; tightness holds at every known point on the line b = a-1 with a >= 3 and k in {3,4}, and FAILS at k = 5 (see rado-r5-a3-b2-frontier), so the prediction is a pattern and not a theorem
would_settle: A refutation of F_1501 (the CNF for n = 1501, k = 4) would give R_4(6(x-y)=5z) = 1501 exactly and complete the k=4 row of the paper's Table 1. Not attempted here: F_313 already required ~28 GiB and a 4096-cell cube cover, and n = 1501 is substantially larger.
frontier.attack_notes: The satisfiable side is closed (the construction hands over the witness free). For the refutation, reuse the 313 recipe at greater depth: branch on more points (depth 8-10), cap per-cell conflicts, defer checking, and certify offline with certify_dumped_cover; distribute cells across s5-s7. The probe suggests concentrating splits inside the staircase-compatible subtree rather than uniformly.

notes: Recorded as the natural next exact-value target (roadmap R10/E1): the construction predicts 741, the k<=4 pattern supports it, SLS cannot refute it, and both certification artifact kinds plus their checkers are now promoted into the axeyum-search crate.
